properties.name: Roma Norte
properties.blurb: Your home base. Tree-lined streets, art-deco apartments, the densest cluster of good cafés and bars in the country. Walk it day or night without a second thought.
tips: Calle Orizaba between Plaza Río de Janeiro and the southern edge is the spine — start there
Coffee at Cucurucho, lunch at Lalo!, late drink at Limantour
Sundays the parks fill with families and dogs — go
Cross to Condesa on Sonora or Veracruz for a different mood, same safety

properties.name: Roma Sur
properties.blurb: Lower-key sibling to Roma Norte. Same safety, fewer foreigners, more affordable lunches. Worth the wander, especially on a slow afternoon.
tips: Mercado Medellín for South American produce and Cuban food counters
Cross north on Tonalá or Orizaba into Roma Norte proper
Quieter at night — fine, just less foot traffic

properties.name: Condesa
properties.blurb: The greenest of the central neighborhoods, organized around two parks. Equal to Roma Norte for safety, slightly more polished, slightly more dog-walker.
tips: Run or walk the Parque México loop at golden hour
Avenida Amsterdam is a ring — follow it for an architecture tour
Tuesday tianguis on Pachuca/Campeche if you're around

properties.name: Juárez / Zona Rosa
properties.blurb: Mixed bag in the best way. Juárez proper is calm and bookish; Zona Rosa is loud, neon, gay-friendly nightlife. Both safe, just different volumes.
tips: Reforma's Sunday closure (ciclovía) passes through — bike or walk it
Lardo and Niddo are sit-down breakfast standouts on the Juárez side
Insurgentes Metro plaza is best skipped late at night, but the streets around are fine

properties.name: Polanco
properties.blurb: Tree-shaded, embassy-quiet, expensive. Masaryk is the high-end shopping spine. Stellar restaurants, formal feel — bring real shoes.
tips: Pujol and Quintonil are here — book weeks ahead
Walk the side streets, not Masaryk itself, for the architecture
Take an Uber back to Roma — it's not walking distance

properties.name: Bosque de Chapultepec
properties.blurb: The park, not a residential zone. Castillo on the hill, Antropología and modern-art museums in the woods. Mostly closed Mondays.
tips: Antropología deserves a half-day minimum
Go Tuesday–Sunday; Mondays nearly everything is shut
Sundays are crowded but free for residents

properties.name: Centro Histórico
properties.blurb: Spectacular by day, rougher after dark. Stick to the main pedestrian streets and the perimeter of the Zócalo. Plan to Uber back to Roma by 9pm.
tips: Madero is pedestrian-only and lined with sights — walk it from Bellas Artes to the Zócalo
Climb the Torre Latino observation deck for the best CDMX panorama
Don't wander north past the cathedral after dark — that's Tepito's edge
Café de Tacuba (the original) for a properly old lunch

properties.name: Doctores
properties.blurb: Working-class, gritty, fine by day if you have a reason. The Arena México (lucha libre) is the main draw and the only reason most visitors set foot here.
tips: Lucha libre on Tuesdays and Fridays — go with a guide or group
Uber in and out, don't street-hail
Skip after dark unless you're at the Arena

properties.name: Coyoacán
properties.blurb: Half-day or full-day trip. Cobblestone streets, Casa Azul, the central plaza with mariachis on weekends. Feels like a colonial town that the city grew around.
tips: Buy Casa Azul tickets online a week+ in advance — they sell out daily
Eat at Mercado de Coyoacán — the tostadas counter is the move
Combine with San Ángel if it's a Saturday

properties.name: San Ángel
properties.blurb: Saturdays, basically. The Bazaar Sábado on Plaza San Jacinto is the reason to come — cobblestones, galleries, antiques, the city's best craft shopping.
tips: Saturday is the day — most of the action is the bazaar
Combine with Coyoacán; they're 15 minutes apart by Uber
Casa Estudio Diego Rivera y Frida Kahlo is here (different from Casa Azul)

properties.name: Xochimilco
properties.blurb: Day trip. The trajineras (painted boats) on the canals are the main event. Touristy but genuinely fun — locals do this too. Bring food and drinks.
tips: Embarcadero Cuemanco or Nuevo Nativitas for less hassle than Fernando Celada
Negotiate the boat price upfront, by the hour
Saturdays are the loudest party; weekdays are calmer
Allow half a day round-trip from Roma

properties.name: Tepito
properties.blurb: Avoid. The city's most famous open-air market, also famously rough. People will tell you it's fine if you blend in. You won't blend in.
tips: Don't pass through, even by Uber
If you're determined, go with a local guide who works that beat
Plenty of grit elsewhere in CDMX without the risk profile
